item.title: The Forgotten First Schoolteacher in Kasilof — Part 2
item.description: AUTHOR’S NOTE: In the early 1920s in New York’s rural Oneida County, the Browne, Cole and Ingersoll families became acquainted. The Coles were raising foxes at Alder Creek. The Brownes were operating a dairy farm in Remsen. And teenagers Marion Ingersoll (from Steuben) and Milton Cole were falling in love. In the mid- to late 1920s, the Brownes and Coles hatched a plan to move to Kasilof, Alaska, acquire a homestead and start fox farming there. Marion Ingersoll tagged along, planning to marry Milton once she reached Alaska. By the end of Part One of this story, the New York pioneers had just arrived in Kasilof. It was late July 1928. Their homestead, in Perry Cole’s name, had been staked; the cabin logs had been cut and peeled; Milton and Marion were married.
